literal: The Hu did not obey orders; more than a thousand men fled in revolt.
idiomatic: The Hu refused their orders, and more than a thousand men broke away in flight.

literal: Jie and Chong attacked, killed them, and took captive several thousand men and women.
idiomatic: Jie and Chong struck, killed them, and took several thousand men and women captive.

literal: Jie was morning and evening at the privy council, deeply entrusted; by nature he was sternly upright, relying on favor to act on his own authority.
idiomatic: Jie spent his days at the privy council, deeply trusted; upright by nature, he leaned on imperial favor and acted on his own authority.

literal: The emperor's heart grew somewhat displeased.
idiomatic: The emperor's heart turned somewhat against him.

literal: When there was discussion of campaigning against the Rouran, Jie did not wish it and said to the emperor: "The barbarians have no settled towns; they migrate without fixed abode. In past campaigns when the army went out, nothing was captured. Better to expand farming and stockpile grain, and await their coming.
idiomatic: When the court debated a campaign against the Rouran, Jie opposed it and told the emperor, "The barbarians have no walled towns; they wander without fixed abode. Every past expedition came back empty-handed. Better to widen the fields and heap up grain, and wait for them to come to us.

literal: " The ministers all followed his counsel.
idiomatic: " The ministers all sided with him.

literal: The emperor decided to go; he then asked Cui Hao, and Hao firmly said they could be attacked.
idiomatic: The emperor resolved to march anyway and asked Cui Hao; Hao insisted they could be attacked.

literal: The emperor followed Hao's counsel.
idiomatic: The emperor followed Hao's advice.

literal: After setting out, he fixed a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley.
idiomatic: Once the army was out, he set a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley.

literal: Jie, resenting that his plan was not used and wishing to thwart the generals, forged an edict changing the date, so the generals did not arrive.
idiomatic: Jie, bitter that his plan was ignored and wanting to thwart the generals, forged an edict and moved the rendezvous, so the generals never came.

literal: At that time the barbarian masses were in great disorder; Crown Prince Jing wished to strike them, but Jie held that it could not be done—the matter is in the imperial annals.
idiomatic: The barbarian hosts were then in turmoil; Crown Prince Jing wanted to strike, but Jie forbade it—the account is in the imperial annals.

literal: They halted at Luhun Valley six days, yet the generals still did not advance.
idiomatic: They waited six days at Luhun Valley, and still the generals did not advance.

literal: [2] The bandits had already fled far; they pursued to Shishui, did not overtake them, and returned.
idiomatic: [2] The enemy had already fled far off; the army chased to Shishui, failed to catch them, and turned back.

literal: The army halted in the desert; provisions were exhausted and many soldiers died.
idiomatic: The army halted in the desert; grain ran out and many soldiers died.

literal: Jie secretly sent men to alarm the army and urged the emperor to abandon the army and return lightly; the emperor did not follow.
idiomatic: Jie secretly had men panic the troops and urged the emperor to abandon the army and ride back lightly; the emperor refused.

literal: Jie, because the campaign had no success, memorialized placing blame on Cui Hao.
idiomatic: Because the campaign had failed, Jie memorialized to lay the blame on Cui Hao.

literal: The emperor said: "The generals were late, and when the bandits came they did not strike—the fault lies with the generals; how could it lie with Hao?
idiomatic: The emperor said, "The generals were late, and when the enemy came they would not strike—the fault is the generals', not Hao's.

literal: " Hao again spoke of Jie's forged edict, and the affair came to light.
idiomatic: " Hao again exposed Jie's forged edict, and the matter broke open.

literal: When the imperial carriage reached Wuyuan, Jie was arrested and imprisoned.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Wuyuan, Jie was seized and imprisoned.

literal: When the emperor set out on campaign, Jie had privately told his kin: "If the army goes out without success and the carriage does not return, I shall set up the Prince of Leyeping.
idiomatic: Before the emperor marched, Jie had told his kin in private, "If the campaign fails and the carriage does not return, I shall set up the Prince of Leyeping.

literal: " Jie also had Right Assistant Director Zhang Song seek prognostic texts and ask: "The Liu house is fated to rule—to succeed the state thereafter; do I in truth have a name and surname?
idiomatic: " Jie also had Right Assistant Director Zhang Song seek prognostic books and ask, "The Liu house is fated to rule and succeed the state—do I truly have a name and surname among them?

literal: " Song replied: "There is a surname but no name.
idiomatic: " Song answered, "There is a surname but no name.

literal: " Under exhaustive investigation confessions were drawn out; they searched Song's house and indeed found the prognostic book.
idiomatic: " Under exhaustive investigation confessions were drawn out; they searched Song's house and indeed found the prognostic book, the annals record.

literal: Jie, the Duke of Nankang Di Lin, Song, and the rest were all exterminated to the third degree; more than a hundred died.
idiomatic: Jie, Duke of Nankang Di Lin, Song, and the rest were all exterminated to the third degree; more than a hundred people died.

literal: Once Jie held a position of power, he monopolized authority and favor; those who fawned on him were promoted, [3] those who crossed him were dismissed, and within and without all feared him—men watched him sidelong.
idiomatic: Once Jie held power he wielded authority and favor at will; flatterers rose, [3] the resentful were cast out, and inside and outside the court all feared him—men watched him sidelong.

literal: Those who stormed cities and broke states heaped up wealth and goods and shared them with Jie.
idiomatic: Men who stormed cities and broke kingdoms heaped up loot and split it with Jie.

literal: When his household goods were inventoried, wealth exceeded tens of millions.
idiomatic: When his household was inventoried, his wealth ran to tens of millions.

literal: The emperor, in retrospective anger, spoke of him with gnashing teeth.
idiomatic: The emperor, looking back in fury, spoke of him with gnashing teeth.

literal: Gu Bi was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Gu Bi came from Dai.

literal: In youth he was loyal and careful, fond of reading books, and also skilled at mounted archery.
idiomatic: As a youth he was loyal and careful, loved books, and was skilled at mounted archery.

literal: At first he was a hunt attendant; sent to Chang'an, he pleased the emperor and was transferred to Palace Memorials, renowned for keen uprightness.
idiomatic: He began as a hunt attendant; sent to Chang'an, he pleased the throne and was moved to palace memorials, famed for sharp integrity.

literal: Taizong commended him and bestowed the name Bi, taking the brush—straight and useful; later the name was changed to Bi, meaning material for assisting.
idiomatic: Taizong praised him and gave him the name Bi, from the writing brush—straight and useful; later the name was fixed as Bi, for one fit to assist.

literal: He ordered Bi to oversee the western secretariat, sharing the pivots of state with Liu Jie and the rest and presenting memorials on the hundred offices.
idiomatic: He put Bi in charge of the western secretariat, sharing the pivots of state with Liu Jie and others and reporting on the hundred offices.

literal: When the emperor succeeded, for merit he was made General Who Establishes Integrity and enfeoffed as Marquis of Lingshou.
idiomatic: When the emperor succeeded, Bi was made General Who Establishes Integrity for his merit and enfeoffed as Marquis of Lingshou.

literal: He campaigned against the rebel Hu of Bingzhou.
idiomatic: He campaigned against the rebel Hu of Bingzhou, the annals record.

literal: On return he was advanced to Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing, overseeing southern memorials.
idiomatic: On his return he was made palace attendant and director of the masters of writing, overseeing southern memorials.

literal: He also received the surrender of the eastern Gaoche at Yini Marsh with Anyuan.
idiomatic: He also received the surrender of the eastern Gaoche at Yini Marsh with Anyuan, the annals record.

literal: He also camped with Liu Jie north of the Yellow River at Wuyuan to guard against rebel people.
idiomatic: He also camped with Liu Jie north of the Yellow River at Wuyuan to guard against rebel subjects.

literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the West and followed the campaign against Helian Ding.
idiomatic: He was named General Who Pacifies the West and followed the campaign against Helian Ding.

literal: When the carriage reached Pingliang, it halted south of Jing.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Pingliang, it halted south of Jing.

literal: He sent Bi with Palace Attendant Zhang Li to attack Pingliang.
idiomatic: He sent Bi with Palace Attendant Zhang Li to strike Pingliang.

literal: Helian Ding himself led twenty thousand foot and horse from Anding to rescue; he met Bi and the rest; Bi feigned retreat to lure him.
idiomatic: Helian Ding himself led twenty thousand foot and horse from Anding to the rescue; meeting Bi and the others, Bi feigned retreat to lure him on.

literal: The emperor sent the Gaoche Tiele to charge Ding at the gallop; several thousand heads were cut off.
idiomatic: The emperor sent the Gaoche Tiele to charge Ding at the gallop; several thousand heads were taken.

literal: Bi pressed the victory and took Anding.
idiomatic: Bi pressed the victory and took Anding, the annals record.

literal: He also with Prince of Yongchang Wang Jian and the rest campaigned against Feng Wentong.
idiomatic: He also joined Prince of Yongchang Wang Jian and others in campaigning against Feng Wentong.

literal: Wentong shut the city and held firm; Bi cut his grain and returned.
idiomatic: Wentong shut the city and held firm; Bi cut his grain crops and withdrew.

literal: Later they again campaigned against Wentong; Wentong begged rescue from Goguryeo.
idiomatic: Later they campaigned against Wentong again; Wentong begged Goguryeo for rescue.

literal: When Goguryeo's rescue arrived, Wentong was about to flee east; the people found it hard to bear.
idiomatic: When Goguryeo's rescue arrived, Wentong was about to flee east, and the people could hardly endure it.

literal: His great minister Gu Lei, because the people's hearts did not wish it, then led the masses to attack Wentong and opened the city gate to bring in the official army.
idiomatic: His great minister Gu Lei, seeing the people would not follow, led the masses against Wentong and opened the gates to admit the imperial army.

literal: Bi suspected Gu Lei of deceit and did not enter the city.
idiomatic: Bi suspected Gu Lei of treachery and would not enter the city.

literal: When the Goguryeo army arrived, Wentong then followed it.
idiomatic: When the Goguryeo army arrived, Wentong went with it.

literal: When Wentong fled, he had women don armor in the center while his picked troops and the Goguryeo arrayed their soldiers outside.
idiomatic: As Wentong fled, he put women in armor in the center while his picked troops and the Goguryeo drew up outside.

literal: Bi's subordinate general Gao Gouzi led cavalry to charge the rebel army; Bi, drunk, drew his sword to stop him, so Wentong was able to flee east.
idiomatic: Bi's subordinate Gao Gouzi led cavalry to charge the rebel host; Bi, drunk, drew his sword to stop him, so Wentong escaped east.

literal: Officers and soldiers all resented that Bi did not strike.
idiomatic: Officers and soldiers alike resented that Bi would not strike.

literal: The emperor was greatly angered, recalled him, and demoted him to gate guard of Guangxia Gate.
idiomatic: The emperor was furious, recalled him, and demoted him to gate guard of Guangxia Gate.

literal: Before long he was again made palace attendant and, with Director of the Masters of Writing Li Shun, was sent as envoy to Liangzhou.
idiomatic: Before long he was palace attendant again and, with Director Li Shun, was sent as envoy to Liangzhou.

literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed as Duke of Jianxing, and stationed at Chang'an with great renown.
idiomatic: He was made General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed as Duke of Jianxing, and stationed at Chang'an with great renown, the annals record.

literal: When they deliberated campaigning against Liangzhou, Bi and Shun both said Liangzhou lacked grass and water and was unsuited to marching an army.
idiomatic: When the court debated a Liangzhou campaign, Bi and Shun both said Liangzhou lacked grass and water and was no place to march an army.

literal: The emperor did not follow.
idiomatic: The emperor would not hear it.

literal: After Guzang was taken, he was somewhat displeased with him, but because he had generalship he did not blame him.
idiomatic: After Guzang fell he bore a slight grudge, yet because Bi had generalship he did not punish him.

literal: Liu Yilong sent general Pei Fangming and others to attack the Prince of Southern Qin Yang Nandang; Nandang sent envoys begging rescue troops.
idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent general Pei Fangming and others against Prince of Southern Qin Yang Nandang; Nandang sent envoys begging for rescue.

literal: Before they arrived, Nandang fled to Shanggui; Fangming took Chouchi and set up Yang Xuan's younger son Baochi.
idiomatic: Before relief came, Nandang fled to Shanggui; Fangming took Chouchi and set up Yang Xuan's younger son Baochi.

literal: Thereupon Bi was given the staff of authority and commanded the armies of Longyou.
idiomatic: Bi was then given the staff of authority and put in command of the armies of Longyou.

literal: Yilong sent his Qinzhou Inspector Hu Chongzhi to hold Chouchi; Bi with General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Qi intercepted Chongzhi at Zhuoshui and captured him in battle; his masses fled back to Hanzhong.
idiomatic: Yilong sent his Qinzhou inspector Hu Chongzhi to hold Chouchi; Bi with General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Qi intercepted Chongzhi at Zhuoshui, seized him in the fight, and his troops fled back to Hanzhong.

literal: Bi and the rest entered from the south of Xiangjiao Mountain with the eastern-route general Pi Baozi and the rest to campaign against Chouchi, sending Marquis of Yong'an He Chun to attack Yilong and block the narrow passes.
idiomatic: Bi and the rest entered from south of Xiangjiao Mountain with eastern-route general Pi Baozi and others against Chouchi, and sent Marquis of Yong'an He Chun to strike Yilong and seal the narrow passes.

literal: The defending general Jiang Daozu withdrew to hold Narrow Pavilion.
idiomatic: The defending general Jiang Daozu fell back to hold Narrow Pavilion.

literal: The generals, because the mountain road was precipitous and at the time snow was deep so horses were inconvenient, all delayed and did not advance.
idiomatic: The generals, finding the mountain road steep and snow deep so horses were useless, all hung back.

literal: Bi alone advanced the army, sent Yuan Qi, He Chun, and the rest to attack Narrow Pavilion; Daozu fled south and Chouchi was pacified.
idiomatic: Bi alone pushed the army forward, sent Yuan Qi, He Chun, and the rest against Narrow Pavilion; Daozu fled south and Chouchi was pacified.

literal: Before long the various Di again set up Yang Wende as lord and besieged Chouchi.
idiomatic: Before long the Di clans again set up Yang Wende as lord and besieged Chouchi.

literal: Bi sent armies from Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qiansheng to campaign against them; [4] the siege of Chouchi was lifted and Wende fled to Hanchuan.
idiomatic: Bi sent armies from Shanggui, Gaoping, and Qiansheng against them; [4] the siege of Chouchi was raised and Wende fled to Hanchuan.

literal: At that time Baozi commanded the Guanzhong armies and halted at Xiabian; hearing Chouchi's siege was lifted, he deliberated returning the army.
idiomatic: Baozi then commanded the Guanzhong armies and halted at Xiabian; hearing Chouchi's siege was lifted, he debated withdrawing.

literal: Bi sent word to Baozi saying: "We have lately broken the rebel armies in succession; I fear their ruler and ministers have not yet grasped the great division, and are shamed by defeat—perhaps they will come to take revenge.
idiomatic: Bi sent word to Baozi, "Having broken the rebel armies in succession, I fear their ruler and ministers have not yet accepted the great division and, shamed by defeat, may come for revenge.

literal: If you withdraw the army, the bandit masses will come again; a later effort will be hard.
idiomatic: If you withdraw now, the enemy will return and a later campaign will be harder.

literal: Better to repair arms and drill troops, store strength, and await them.
idiomatic: Better to repair arms, drill the troops, store your strength, and wait.

literal: Before autumn and winter are out, the southern bandits will surely come; to await the weary with the rested is the strategy of a hundred victories.
idiomatic: Before autumn and winter are out the southern enemy will surely come; to meet the weary with the rested is the strategy of a hundred victories.

literal: " Baozi then stopped.
idiomatic: " Baozi then held his ground.

literal: The emperor heard of it and said: "Bi's words are a long-range plan.
idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he said, "Bi's words are the long view.

literal: In controlling Southern Qin, Bi's stratagems were many."
idiomatic: In holding Southern Qin, Bi's stratagems were many."

literal: When Crown Prince Jing took overall charge of the myriad affairs, Bi was summoned as one of the Eastern Palace's four supports, joining Prince of Yidu Mu Shou and the rest in participating in government.
idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jing took overall charge of affairs, Bi was summoned as one of the Eastern Palace's four supports, joining Prince of Yidu Mu Shou and others in government.

literal: An edict made Bi tutor to the Eastern Palace; for mature, steady service he was given a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand jin of cotton.
idiomatic: An edict made Bi tutor to the Eastern Palace; for mature, steady service he was given a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand jin of cotton, the annals record.

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the masters of writing.

literal: Though Bi's duties were pressing, he never ceased reading; correct, careful, and close-mouthed, he never spoke of inner-palace affairs; his fame and merit equaled Zhang Li's but his integrity did not.
idiomatic: Though his duties pressed hard, Bi never stopped reading; correct, careful, and close-mouthed, he never spoke of inner-palace affairs; his fame and merit matched Zhang Li's, but not his integrity.

literal: People of Shanggu submitted a memorial saying the parks and preserves were excessive, the people had no fields to farm, and begging to reduce them by more than half to bestow on the poor.
idiomatic: Men of Shanggu memorialized that the parks and preserves were excessive, the people had no land to farm, and begged to cut them by more than half for the poor.

literal: Bi read it; [5] he entered wishing to memorialize but met the emperor playing go with Attendant of the Masters of Writing Liu Shu, with no mind for affairs.
idiomatic: Bi read it; [5] he entered to memorialize but found the emperor playing go with Attendant Liu Shu, with no mind for business.

literal: Bi sat in attendance a long while and could not make his report heard.
idiomatic: Bi sat in attendance a long while and could not get a hearing.

literal: He then rose, before the emperor seized Shu's head, dragged him off the couch, struck his ears with his hand and beat his back with his fist, saying: "The court does not govern—it is truly your crime!
idiomatic: He rose, seized Shu's head before the emperor, dragged him off the couch, boxed his ears and beat his back, crying, "The court does not govern—and the fault is yours!

literal: " The emperor lost composure, set down the go stones, and said: "Not to hear memorials is truly in my person—what crime has Shu?
idiomatic: " The emperor lost composure, set down the stones, and said, "Not hearing memorials is my fault—what crime has Shu?

literal: Release him!
idiomatic: Let him go!

literal: " Bi set forth the full circumstances in a report.
idiomatic: " Bi laid the full case before him.

literal: The emperor marveled at Bi's public uprightness and approved all he memorialized, granting it to the common people.
idiomatic: The emperor marveled at Bi's blunt integrity, approved all he had urged, and granted the land to the people.

literal: Bi said: "For a minister to vent his will before his lord is not without guilt.
idiomatic: Bi said, "For a minister to vent his will before his lord is not without guilt.

literal: " He then went to the Masters of Carts, removed cap and shoes, and impeached himself begging punishment.
idiomatic: " He went to the masters of carts, removed cap and shoes, and impeached himself, begging punishment.

literal: The emperor sent an envoy to summon him.
idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to summon him, the annals record.

literal: When he arrived, the emperor said: "Put on cap and shoes.
idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor said, "Put on cap and shoes.

literal: I have heard that in the work of building an altar, one limps yet builds it, yet attends it in full regalia, and the spirits bless it.
idiomatic: I have heard that in building an altar one may limp yet still build it, yet attend it in full regalia—and the spirits bless it.

literal: Then what crime have you?
idiomatic: What crime have you, then?

literal: From now on, whatever profits the altars of state, benefits the realm and eases the people—even if you are overturned and rushed—you shall do it without regard."
idiomatic: From now on, whatever profits the altars of state and eases the people—even in overturn and haste—you shall do it without looking back."

literal: The emperor held a great review and was about to hunt in Hexi with his officers.
idiomatic: The emperor held a great review and was about to hunt in Hexi with his officers, the annals record.

literal: Bi remained on guard; an edict ordered fat horses given to the mounted men, but Bi ordered the weak ones given.
idiomatic: Bi remained on guard; an edict ordered fat horses for the mounted men, but Bi gave them the weak ones.

literal: The emperor was greatly angered and said: "Pointed-head slave, you dare measure me!
idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and cried, "Pointed-head slave—you dare measure me!
